title: Clear the Mech3 narrative-cite Stage-2 dangling references: drive bogus-anchor (35) + file-missing (20) to zero and resolve-rate (46.1%) back over the 85% acceptance bar. Fix the pointers, do not game the metric.
goal: Get audit-narrative-citations.js Stage 2 back to GREEN. Current 2026-08-02T08:10 workspace-sync report: citation-resolve-rate 46.1% (target >=85%), bogus-anchor 35 (cap <=20), file-missing 20 (cap <=20, at the line). These are the ACTIONABLE half of the standing Mech3 RED — a small, bounded set of real dangling pointers, distinct from the Stage-1 threshold debate (see DIRECTIVE-20260802-002).

context.operator_framing: Operator (2026-08-02, via cowork): the Stage-1 95.8% claim-uncited number is a threshold-realism question routed separately (DIRECTIVE-20260802-002). THIS directive is only the Stage-2 dangling-reference cleanup: citations that DO exist but don't resolve. 35 bogus anchors + 20 missing files is a concrete, finite worklist worth clearing — real broken references an agent wrote that point at a key or path that isn't there.
context.what_stage2_checks: Per audit-narrative-citations.js Stage 2: for each citation carrying a ':<field-anchor>' tail, verify the cited file exists AND (for JSON) contains a key matching the anchor anywhere in the tree; for .md/.txt the anchor is checked as a literal substring. 'bogus-anchor' = file exists but anchor key/substring absent. 'file-missing' = cited path does not resolve (after WELL_KNOWN_PATHS auto-resolution). Acceptance (PROP-069 recalibrated): resolve-rate >=85%, bogus-anchor <=20, file-missing <=20.
context.surfaces_in_scope: The audited surfaces are agent-authored prose fields (e.g. tinker findings[].description at moderate+ severity, kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim). The dangling refs live in those, NOT in the public docs/ pages.
context.immutability_caveat_to_resolve: Some audited surfaces may be immutable/append-only historical records (forensic reports). Determine per-offender whether the citation lives in a LIVE editable surface (fix the anchor/path in place) or an already-archived immutable record (in which case the fix is forward-looking — repoint the anchor's TARGET if the target file moved/renamed, and/or correct the generator so future emissions resolve). Do not rewrite immutable history to launder the metric; fix the real breakage.

task.part_A_itemize: Run audit-narrative-citations.js (or add a --list/emit flag if it doesn't already dump offenders) to produce the itemized list of all 35 bogus-anchor and 20 file-missing citations: surface file, field, the raw '(path:anchor)' citation, and why it fails (missing file vs absent anchor).
task.part_B_classify_each: For each offender, classify the root cause: (1) target file moved/renamed → repoint citation or restore the WELL_KNOWN_PATHS/auto-resolve mapping; (2) anchor key renamed/removed in the target JSON → correct the anchor; (3) genuine typo in the citation; (4) target legitimately gone (evidence deleted) → remove the dead citation with a one-line note; (5) generator bug — an agent prompt/template emits a citation shape that never resolves → fix upstream so it stops re-accruing.
task.part_C_fix: Apply the fixes. Prefer repointing to the real target over deleting. Delete a citation only when the referenced evidence is genuinely gone, and note it. Where the root cause is a generator (category 5), fix the emitting prompt/script so the class stops regenerating — that is the durable win.
task.part_D_verify_green: Re-run the audit; confirm resolve-rate >=85% (target: near 100%), bogus-anchor and file-missing both well under the <=20 caps (target: 0). Include the before/after counts.

constraints.no_metric_gaming: Do NOT satisfy the bar by bulk-deleting citations, loosening the checker, widening WELL_KNOWN_PATHS to swallow real breakage, or relaxing the anchor match. Fix pointers to actually resolve. Removing a citation is allowed ONLY for genuinely-dead targets, individually noted.
constraints.archives_are_sacred: Do not alter *-archive.jsonl durable records to change the metric. If an offender lives in an immutable archive, the fix is repointing the target or fixing the generator, not editing the archive.
constraints.stage1_out_of_scope: Do NOT touch the Stage-1 claim-uncited threshold, the claim-shape filter, or the surface list here — that is DIRECTIVE-20260802-002. Keep the two clean and separate.
constraints.apply_path: If any fix targets a NEVER_PUSH surface, ship behind the usual PROP review and operator applies. Clean git-owned data fixes can follow tinker's normal apply path.

deliverable_acceptance_criteria: Itemized before-list of all 35 bogus-anchor + 20 file-missing offenders with per-offender root-cause classification.
Fixes applied (repoint/correct/remove-with-note/generator-fix), each mapped to its offender.
Post-fix audit re-run showing resolve-rate >=85% (ideally ~100%), bogus-anchor and file-missing at/near 0.
If any generator (category 5) was found, the upstream fix that stops the class from re-accruing.
A verification_pattern so a later run can confirm Stage 2 stays green.
operator_notes: Operator (2026-08-02): 'yes to both (probably two separate tinker directives).' This is directive 1 of 2 — the concrete Stage-2 dangling-ref cleanup. Directive 2 (DIRECTIVE-20260802-002) handles the Stage-1 threshold policy question. Keep them independent so the cleanup can land without waiting on the policy call.
